Cheteshwar Pujara gives a little insight on his Day 3's innings. He says although he didn't get many runs earlier, he was confident. Adds that he missed out on a hundred but he is content with the runs he scored. Asserts that playing in the county season was challenging but it was a good preparation for him. States the obvious that Virat Kohli is a great player and no one can play the drives like he does, that too in England. On Ashwin's fitness, Pujara hopes that he stays fit as he is getting the ball to turn considerably. Ends by saying that the pitch has uneven bounce and both spin and pace will come into the fore.

Sanjay Manjrekar reports from the pitch and says the grass it had on Days 1 and 2 has gone considerably. Adds that the surface looks dry underneath and looks difficult for batting. Further adds that there are a lot of rough patches on both sides of the track but it shouldn't excite the bowlers too much as it is on a shortish length. Ends by saying that the deterioration on the pitch is likely to assist the seamers as well as the spinners.

For India, Ashwin is also carrying a niggle it seems. He wasn't on the field much on Day 2 and even yesterday, he was bowling a bit gingerly. Also, if luck favors the home team, even the weather could play a vital role in shielding England from a defeat, in their own backyard. Let us see how the day unfolds. The play starts in a short while, keep a cuppa handy and stay tuned.

Hello and welcome to the fourth day of the third Test between England and India. It's overcast in Nottingham but the sun is shining brightly on the visitors currently. It will be fair to say that India have a firm grip on this match, that too within the first three days. Now, the three main things that the home team will need to battle against during this steep run chase are - a world record chase, unfavorable batting conditions and last but not the least, the unfortunate finger injury to Bairstow who is unlikely to bat.
... Day 4, Session 1 ...

England, on the other hand, will have to take it session by session. The injury to Jonny Bairstow has added to their woes. It is going to be an uphill task for them and they will have to bat out of their skin if they are to pull off a miracle. So, what is in store for us - India continuing their domination or England fighting back? Join us at 1100 local (1000 GMT) to find out on Day 4. Till then goodbye and take care.

The Indian batsmen have done their job and now the onus is on their bowlers to do the rest. They will come out fresh tomorrow and try and repeat their first innings performance. The pitch has still plenty to offer and the Indian bowlers will want to make use of it.

The visitors are still way ahead in the contest, courtesy, Kohli and Pujara who stitched a 113-run stand. The two took their time, got their eye in and then flourished as the day progressed. Pujara was unfortunate to not get a century whereas the Indian skipper, this time, got to his 23rd Test ton. Pandya's cameo was the icing on the cake which helped them take the lead over the 500-run mark.

So, the English openers have survived the nervy period and will head into Day 4 unscathed. Exactly what they would have wanted after being set a massive target. India though would have loved to get a wicket or two before Stumps. Anyway, they bowled well but just could not find the edge.
And he negotiates it well! Another cheer from the crowd as Cook safely blocks this ball on middle. STUMPS ON DAY 3!
That's the slider on off, Cook prods forward and blocks it. A loud cheer from the crowd, now only one more ball to survive the day.
Two balls to go and Virat Kohli wants the helmet to be brought out. He wants an extra fielder close-in.
Slower through the air on off, the batsman lunges and blocks it out.
Close! This is bowled quicker, it pitches and skids through. Cook at the very end gets his bat down and works it to square leg.
On the pads, tucked around the corner with the angle.
Flatter on off, Cook goes back and keeps it out.
Fuller on off, it is crisply driven to the man at covers.
Almost drags it on! Short and outside off, Jennings tries to punch it through the off side but due to the slow nature of the pitch, he gets an inside edge towards the keeper.

How many times have we seen the ball beat the bat today? First it was the English bowlers and now the Indians. On a length around off, this one also straightens. Jennings tries to block it but gets beaten.
On a length around off, Jennings leaves it alone. The umpire has a word there with Ishant as he is getting close to the danger area.
Fuller on the pads, Keaton flicks it but finds the square leg fielder.
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads.
NO BALL! Ishant has overstepped as he bends his back on this one. Bangs it short, it skids through and hits Jennings on his gloves.
A little too full so the turn is out of contention. Cook pushes it towards covers.
Flatter this time on off, Cook keeps it out.
Nice! Encouraging stuff for Ashwin. He gets turn and bounce. He floats this up on off, it pitches and then turns away, beating the outside edge of Cook's bat.
Down the leg side, Cook tries to flick but misses.
Gives this air on off, Cook defends it.
A little too short to begin with. On the pads, Cook whips it through mid-wicket and the batsmen run two.
Ravichandran Ashwin is into the attack. He has two slips and a short leg in place.
A little too wide outside off, the batsman does not bother playing at it.
Good leave! Around off, Jennings shoulders arms to it.
Attacks the stumps, Jennings gets behind the line and defends it.
Angles this on the pads, Jennings tries to flick but misses to get hit on the pads.
Play and a miss again! On a length around off, straightens after pitching. Jennings plays inside the line and gets beaten.
Very full on middle, Jennings hits it towards mid on.
Shorter again on off, Cook jumps and blocks it.
On the off pole, Cook defends it out.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.

FOUR! Bread and butter stuff for Cook! On the pads, he flicks it through mid-wicket and another boundary results. England are doing well here by making the scoring opportunities count. To not get bogged down in such a massive run chase is very vital.

WOW! How has that missed the outside edge first and then the stumps? Bumrah angles this into the off pole. It pitches and then shapes away. Cook, rooted to his crease, tries to block it out but gets beaten.
Nicely played! Short of a length on off, Cook stands tall and punches it through covers. The batsmen run two.
Outside off again, Jennings lets it be.
The batsman shoulders arms to let that one through.
Outside off, left alone.
Another very good delivery! Full and swinging away. Cook guides it towards point and gets to the other end. He is off the mark.
Good length on off, Cook guides it towards gully who makes a good stop diving to his left.
Good deliver, outside off and on a length. Cook watchfully lets it be.
The batsman has driven it through mid on.
FOUR! Dealing in boundaries is Jennings. Back of a length around off, Keaton opens the face of the bat and guides it through third man. He has scored all of England's run so far.
OHHHH! This is pitched around off, from around the wicket. It skids through. Jennings tries to block it but gets an inside edge onto his pads.
Using the pace here is Jennings! Full again on off, no swing on offer. Jennings times it through mid off and gets another couple.
FOUR! Need not run for those! First boundary of this innings. Bumrah bowls it a touch too full and outside off, Keaton strokes it through cover-point and the ball races away.
Back of a length on off, Jennings stands tall and defends it onto the ground.
Slightly outside off, Cook need not play at those.
On the off pole, the batsman drops it towards covers and gets to the other end.

Terrific delivery! He got Cook with a similar delivery in the first innings and almost got Jennings here. On a length and around off, it pitches and then shapes away. Jennings, with no foot movement, tries to block but is beaten.

Good cricket all around again! Ishant angles it into the batsman first and then gets the ball to shape away. Jennings first thinks of playing at it due to the original trajectory but seeing the swing, he shoulders arms.
Ishant goes fuller but the ball does not seam or swing. Keaton leans into it and strokes it through mid off for a couple.
On a length around off, Jennings keeps it out.
Ishant Sharma has been given the new ball. He will bowl from the other end.
Well bowled and well played! Another delivery on a length, this one stays a touch low. Cook at the very end, brings his bat down and blocks it. End of a very good first over by Bumrah.
On off and angling away. Cook makes the third leave of the over.
Tries to repeat the same delivery he bowled on the last ball but this is a touch shorter. Cook defends it.
Absolute gem there by Bumrah! He bowls this on a length and around off, it pitches and then moves away. Cook tries to block it out by hopping but is beaten.
Slightly fuller outside off, no swing on offer. Cook makes another leave.
Starts off with a length ball outside off, does not take off after pitching. Cook shoulders arms to it.
